questions.text: Alpha and Beta each invested Rs. 10,000 for 2 years at the same rate of interest of 10% p.a., but Beta’s investment is compounded annually and Alpha’s investment is charged on simple interest. What amount did Beta receive more than Alpha?

options.text: More than one of the above

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Rs 100.

Key Points Simple interest is calculated using the formula:

Simple Interest = Principal × Rate × Time
In this case, the principal is Rs. 10,000, the rate is 10% p.a., and the time is 2 years. Therefore, Alpha's simple interest would be:

Simple Interest = Rs. 10,000 × 10% × 2 years = Rs. 2,000
Beta's Compound Interest (Annual Compounding):

Compound interest is calculated by compounding the interest earned each period. In this case, the interest is compounded annually. The formula for compound interest is:

Amount = Principal × (1 + Rate/Number of Compounding Periods)^Number of Periods
In this case, the principal is Rs. 10,000, the rate is 10% p.a., the number of compounding periods is 2 (since the interest is compounded annually), and the number of periods is also 2 (since the investment period is 2 years). Therefore, Beta's compound interest would be:

Amount = Rs. 10,000 × (1 + 10%/2)^2 = Rs. 2,100
Difference in Amount Received:

To determine the difference in the amount received by Alpha and Beta, we subtract Alpha's simple interest from Beta's compound interest:

Difference = Beta's Compound Interest - Alpha's Simple Interest
Substituting the calculated values, we get:

Difference = Rs. 2,100 - Rs. 2,000 = Rs. 100
Therefore, Beta received Rs. 100 more than Alpha due to the difference in compounding methods.

questions.text: Keya borrows Rs 25000 from shree at 10% compound rate of interest. At the end of each year she pays Rs 8000 back to shree. At the end of year 3 how much amount would be left for her to pay?
questions.explanation:
Formula used:

C.I= P ((1 + (r / 100)) N -1))

Where, P = Principal amount,

R = Rate of interest

N = Number of years

Calculation:

Amount to be paid at end of year 1 = 25000 × (1 + 0.10)

⇒ Amount = 27500

⇒ P for Year 2 = 27500 – 8000

⇒ P = 19500

⇒ A for year 2 = 19500 × 1.10

⇒ A = 21450

⇒ P for year 3 = 21450 – 8000

⇒ P = 13450

⇒ A for year 3 = 13450 × 1.10

⇒ A = 14795

⇒ P for year 4 = 14795 – 8000

⇒ P for year 4 = 6795

∴ at end of year 3 keya will have to pay Rs 6795 to shree

questions.text: A sum of money amounts to Rs. 3600 in 4 years and Rs. 5400 in 6 years on a certain rate of compound interest. What will be the amount after 10 years with the same rate of interest?
questions.explanation:
Given:

Amount after 4 years = Rs. 3600

Amount after 6 years = Rs. 5400

Formula used:

A = \({\rm{P\;}}{\left( {1{\rm{\;}} + \frac{{\rm{r}}}{{100}}} \right)^{\rm{n}}}{\rm{\;}}\)

here, A = Principal + Interest

P = Principal

r = rate of interest

n = no. of years

Calculation:

Rs. 3600 = \({\rm{P\;}}{\left( {1 + \frac{{\rm{r}}}{{100}}} \right)^4}\)      ----(i)

Rs. 5400 = \({\rm{P\;}}{\left( {1 + \frac{{\rm{r}}}{{100}}} \right)^6}\)      ----(ii)

⇒ From (ii) ÷ (i) we get

⇒ \(\frac{{5400}}{{3600}} = \frac{{{\rm{P}}{{\left( {1 + \frac{{\rm{r}}}{{100}}} \right)}^6}}}{{{\rm{P}}{{\left( {1 + \frac{{\rm{r}}}{{100}}} \right)}^4}}}{\rm{\;}}\)

⇒ \(\frac{3}{2} = {\rm{\;}}{\left( {1 + \frac{{\rm{r}}}{{100}}} \right)^2}\)

\({\left( {1 + \frac{{\rm{r}}}{{100}}} \right)^4}\) = (3/2)2

Now, after 10 years the amount

Amount = \({\rm{P\;}}{\left( {1 + \frac{{\rm{r}}}{{100}}} \right)^{10}}\) = \({\rm{P\;}}{\left( {1 + \frac{{\rm{r}}}{{100}}} \right)^6}\) \({\left( {1 + \frac{{\rm{r}}}{{100}}} \right)^4}\)

A = 5400 (3/2)2 = Rs. 12150

∴ Amount will be Rs. 12150

Shortcut Trick

3600 in 4 years

5400 in 6 years

Ratio of 2 years = 2 : 3

Ratio of 4 years = 4 : 9

⇒ 5400 × 9/4 = Rs. 12150

∴ After ten years amount will be Rs. 12150

questions.text: A principal amount of Rs. 3000 is invested for two years, giving a compound interest of Rs. 967.5. Find the compound interest compounded semi-annually at the same rate of interest on the same principal amount for 1 year.
questions.explanation:
Given:

The principal amount of Rs. 3000 is invested for two years

Compound interest earned = Rs. 967.5 Rs. 

Formula used:

Compound interest = P(1 + R/100)T - P

P = Principal , R = interest rate , T = time

Calculation:

⇒ 967.5 = 3000 × (1 + R/100)2 - 3000

⇒ 1.3225 = (1 + R/100)2

⇒ 1.15 = 1 + R/100

⇒ R = 15

Now,

For half-yearly compound interest calculation

P = 3000, R = 15/2 = 7.5, T = 1 × 2 = 2

So compound interest = 3000 × (1 + 7.5/100)2 - 3000

⇒ 3000 × (43/40)2 - 3000

⇒ 466.875 Rs. ≈ 466.88 Rs

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

questions.text: Rahul invested Rs. 20,000 with rate of interest at 10% per annum. The interest was compounded half yearly for first year and in the next year it was compounded yearly. What will be the total interest earned at the end of two years?
questions.explanation:
Given:

Invested amount = 20000

Rate of interest = 10% p.a.

Concept:

For the first year compounded half yearly and for the second year compounded yearly

Calculation:

Amount = [20000 × (1 + (5/ 100))2 × (1 + (10/100))]

⇒ Amount = 20000 × (21/20) × (21/20) × (11 /10)

⇒ Amount = 24,255

∴ Compound interest = Amount – Principle

⇒ 24255 – 20000 = 4255

questions.text: Sounak and Rounak each invested a certain amount of money in the ratio 3 ∶ 4 at a compound interest rate of 20% and 30% per year, respectively. They collected Rs. 8160 in total interest after two years. Find the sum invested by Rounak.
questions.explanation:
Concept used:

We can use the successive method

a + b + (ab/100)

Calculation:

Let the sum invested by Sounak be 300x

So, interest received by him = 300x × {20 + 20 + (20 × 20)/100} = 132x

Let the sum invested by Rounak be 400x

So, interest received by him = 400x × {30 + 30 + (30 × 30)/100} = 276x

So, the total interest = (132x + 276x) = 408x

As per the question, we can say,

408x = 8160

⇒ x = 20

So, Rounak's investment = 400x = (400 × 20) = 8000

∴ The sum invested by Rounak is Rs. 8000.

Alternate Method

Given:

The ratio between the sum invested by Sounak and Rounak respectively is 3 ∶ 4

Sounak invested at the rate of 20% per annum compounded annually 

Rounak invested at the rate of 30% per annum compounded annually 

The total interest received by them is Rs. 8160

The total time period is 2 years

Formula used:

C.I = P[{1 + (R/100)}n - 1]

Where C.I = Compound interest, P = Principal, R = Rate, n = total time period

Calculation:

Here, Total C.I = Rs. 8160

R = 20%, 30%

t = 2 years

Let Sounak's sum be 3x and Rounak's sum be 4x

Let interest received by Sounak and Rounak be C.IS and C.IR respectively,

Now, according to the question, we can say

C.IS = 3x[{1 + (20/100)}2 - 1]

⇒ C.IS = 3x × (44/100)

C.IR = 4x[{1 + (30/100)}2 - 1]

⇒ C.IR = 4x × (69/100)

Now, again we can say,

[3x × (44/100) + 4x × (69/100)] = 8160

⇒ [(12x/100) × (23 + 11)] = 8160

⇒ [(12x/100) × 34] = 8160

⇒ x = 2000

Rounak's sum = 4x = 4 × 2000 = 8000

∴ The sum invested by Rounak is Rs. 8000.

questions.text: A sum of Rs. 10,000 is borrowed by Akshit for 2 years at an interest of 10% compounded annually. Find the compound interest and amount he has to pay at the end of 2 years.
questions.explanation:
Given:

Principal (P) = Rs. 10,000

Rate of interest (R) = 10%

Time (T) = 2 years

Formula Used:

Compound Interest (CI) = P (1 + R/100)T - P

Amount (A) = P + CI

Calculation:

Step 1: Calculate the amount after 2 years.

⇒ A = 10,000 (1 + 10/100)2

⇒ A = 10,000 (1 + 0.10)2

⇒ A = 10,000 (1.10)2

⇒ A = 10,000 × 1.21

⇒ A = 12,100

Step 2: Calculate the compound interest.

⇒ CI = A - P

⇒ CI = 12,100 - 10,000

⇒ CI = 2,100

The compound interest is Rs. 2,100 and the amount he has to pay at the end of 2 years is Rs. 12,100.

questions.text: Find the amount of compound interest, if the sum of money borrowed is Rs 10,000 for 2 years and rate of interest is 4 % per annum compounded annually for the first year and 6 % per annum compound annually for the second year.
questions.explanation:
Given:

Principal = RS 5,000; T = 2 years; R1 = 4 %; R2 = 6 %

To find:

Amount = ?

Formula used:

A = P(1 + R1 %)(1 + R2 %)

Calculation:

A = P(1 + R1 %)(1 + R2 %)

= 10,000 (1+ 4 %) ( 1 + 6 %)

= Rs 11,024

C.I = Amount – Principal

= Rs (11,024 – 10,000)

= Rs 1,024

questions.text: A sum of Rs. 20,000 is invested at compound interest for 2 years at two different rates of interest of 10% per annum for the first year and 5% per annum for the next year. Find the compound interest earned after two years.
questions.explanation:
Given:

A sum of Rs. 20000 is invested at compound interest for 2 years

Rate of interest = 10% per annum first year and 5% per annum second year

Formula Used:

Compound Interest = P(1 + R/100)N – P

P = principal, R = rate of interest and N = time

Calculation:

Compound Interest = P(1 + R/100)N – P

Compound interest = 20000(1 + 10/100) × (1 + 5/100) – 20000

⇒ 20000 × (110/100 × 105/100) – 20000

⇒ 3100

∴ Compound interest earned after two years is Rs. 3100

questions.text: Banks decided to reduce the interest rate of money deposited with them from 8% to 5% in lieu of COVID-19. If Ram deposited Rs. 8 lakh and after one year, the rate reduction was implemented, then find how much will be his loss at the end of 3 years from depositing at simple interest.
questions.explanation:
Given:

Initial interest rate = 8%

Interest rate after reduction = 5%

Amount Ram deposited = Rs. 8 lakh

Formula used:

Simple interest = PRT/100

Calculation:

For the first year, rate of interest = 8%

Interest obtained for first-year = 8,00,000 × 1 × 8/100 = Rs. 64,000

Interest obtained for 2nd and 3 rd years = 8,00,000 × 2 × 5/100 = Rs. 80,000

Interest he will get for 3 years if 8% was used = 3 × 64,000 = Rs. 1,92,000

Amount he lost due to reduction = 1,92,000 - (64,000 + 80,000) = Rs. 48,000

Alternate Method

Amount he lost due to reduction = 2 years × 3% of Rs. 8,00,000 = Rs. 48,000

∴ The amount he lost due to reduction is Rs. 48,000.
